items.title: Sanusi says Kedah may hold Penang ‘lease’ claim until Perikatan takes Putrajaya
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 10 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said the state is considering delaying its claim for higher Penang “lease” payments, and instead wait for a Perikatan Nasional (PN) takeover of the federal government. According to The Star , Sanusi said Putrajaya had yet to respond positively to Kedah’s demand despite the state pursuing a review of the payments for the past six years. “If the federal government remains stubborn and refuses to pay or consider Kedah’s application, we will change the federal government,” he was quoted as saying.

items.title: Guan Eng questions Penang PH silence over Reezal's remarks
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today questioned Penang PH leaders' silence over Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican's remarks on Umno-DAP ties. Lim said Penang PH's unconditional endorsement of Umno's role in the state government, without responding to Reezal's remarks, was "incomprehensible". "Penang PH top leaders' unconditional endorsement of Umno's role in the Penang government without any response to the unfriendly attacks by the Umno Bertam assemblyman on DAP and PKR is incomprehensible," he said today.

items.title: Four laws to reshape Malaysia's housing sector under new policy
items.summary: The four legislative measures are an expanded Property Development Act, a new Building Managers Act, a new Residential Tenancy Act and amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013. Speaking at a press conference after the launch of the National Housing Policy today, Nga said the existing Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Act 1966 (Act 118) was no longer sufficient as its scope was limited to residential properties. This new act (Property Development Act) will provide a comprehensive legal framework to move the country forward," he said.

items.title: Penang grants Jelutong landfill extension until Oct 2026, project faces scrutiny over EIA concerns
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Penang state government has granted PLB Engineering Berhad (PLBE) an extension of time (EOT) until October 18 for its proposed RM1 billion Jelutong landfill rehabilitation and development project. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the developer’s application for an extension was presented to the state executive council on August 5. “Based on the presentation, the state government decided that an extension of time be granted until October 18, 2026,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: German shippers warn Rhine could be 'split in two' by low water
items.summary: BERLIN: Low water levels risk halting cargo traffic on a key stretch of the Rhine this week, effectively splitting the critical waterway into two separate zones, the federal association of German inland shipping (BDB) said on Monday. "Commercial shipping will no longer be able to transport goods in the region at such low water levels," he said. Last Thursday, the country's inland navigation agency said low water levels on the river Rhine pose increasing problems and costs for freight shipping.

items.title: 30 years on Everest, 'Green Boots' set to be brought home
items.summary: LADAKH, India: The remains of an Indian climber believed to have died on Mount Everest 30 years ago are set to be brought home to his family, the BBC reported. A specialist Indian recovery team is preparing for a high-risk mission to retrieve the remains, believed to be those of Dorje Morup, 48, who died in a snowstorm while descending from the summit in May 1996. The body, known as "Green Boots", was identified earlier this year.

items.title: MRCB, Teco team up on AI-ready modular data centres
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) has teamed up with Taiwan-based Teco Electric & Machinery Co Ltd to develop artificial intelligence (AI)-ready modular data centres (MDCs). MRCB said the MDCs will serve as a testbed to assess the technical and commercial viability of Teco's modular data centre technology, with the potential for similar developments across its landbank. Teco, meanwhile, will provide modular data centre technology, specialised engineering solutions and operational management for the project.

items.title: Contractor fined RM25,000 for failing to ensure construction site safety
items.summary: Judge Irwan Suainbon imposed the fine on C.Y.C. Management Sdn Bhd director Lo Chee Leong, 64, after considering the facts of the occupational safety and health case. He was charged under Regulation 19(3) of the Occupational Safety and Health (Construction Work) (Design and Management) Regulations 2024, under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, punishable under Regulation 19(6) of the same regulations.

items.title: Sand unit price index rises 0.1 to 14.9pct nationwide in July
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The unit price index of sand increased in July 2026, ranging from 0.1 per cent to 14.9 per cent nationwide, compared to the previous month, said the Statistics Department. "The unit price index of steel also edged up slightly in July 2026, ranging from 0.6 per cent to 0.9 per cent month-on-month (MoM). "The highest increase in the price index for the material was recorded in Perak (0.9 per cent), followed by Tawau, Sabah (0.7 per cent), and Sandakan, Sabah (0.6 per cent)," it said.

items.title: Malaysia must build talent fast to keep pace with AI, says Akmal
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping jobs and industries, making early talent development critical to Malaysia's economic ambitions, said Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said 86 per cent of employers also expected AI and information-processing technologies to transform their business operations. Akmal said Malaysia therefore needed to strengthen its talent pipeline to support the country's transition towards high-growth, high-value industries, particularly the semiconductor sector.

items.title: Malaysia's July palm oil stocks rose 3.32pct - MPOB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's July palm oil stocks rose 3.32 per cent from the previous month to 2.63 million tonnes, data from the industry regulator showed on Monday. Crude palm oil production gained 9.41 per cent from June to 1.79 million tonnes, while palm oil exports surged 14.5 per cent to 1.39 million tonnes, the Malaysian Palm Oil Board said. A Reuters survey had forecast inventories at 2.61 million tonnes, with output seen at 1.76 million tonnes and exports at 1.38 million tonnes.

items.title: Penang grants PLB Engineering extension until Oct 18 for Jelutong landfill project
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government has granted PLB Engineering Bhd (PLBE) an extension until Oct 18 to complete outstanding requirements for its Jelutong landfill project. State Local Government, Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the extension was approved by the state executive council at its meeting on Aug 5. The latest extension granted by the state government runs until Oct 18.

items.title: TH reforms yield results as investment, profit distribution improved – Economist
items.summary: Putra Business School MBA Programme director Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said the development forms part of TH's reforms, including the implementation of the Royal Commission of Inquiry's (RCI) recommendations. He said TH had implemented more than 75 per cent of the 25 RCI recommendations completed during TH's governance transformation and recovery phase. "Depositors' savings in TH are definitely safe and secure.

items.title: 16-year-old boy admits to raping, sexually assaulting schoolgirl in library toilet
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A 16-year-old student pleaded guilty at the Magistrate's Court today to raping and sexually assaulting a female schoolgirl in a library toilet The accused entered the plea after the two charges were read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno. He was charged with raping and sexually assaulting the 16-year-old girl at a library toilet at 1.30pm on May 7. The report led to the accused's arrest.

items.title: Intra-Asean trade must rise beyond 25pct, says Mohamad Hasan
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Asean must increase trade among its member states, which currently accounts for less than 25 per cent of the bloc's total trade, if the region is to fully realise its potential as one of the world's largest economies. "We want to see trade among Asean countries increase because, as of today, intra-Asean trade does not exceed 25 per cent. "This will further facilitate the trade that we want to increase among Asean member states," he said.

items.title: Sony, TSMC to spend US$6.3bil to jointly make image sensors, Nikkei says
items.summary: TOKYO: Sony Group and Taiwan's TSMC plan to spend around one trillion yen (US$6.32 billion) to jointly make next-generation microchips used in image sensors, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday. The two tech giants said in May they planned to form a joint venture in Japan to develop and manufacture next-generation image sensors, combining Sony's sensor design expertise with TSMC's manufacturing and process technology strengths. Sony is the world's largest maker of image sensors widely used in smartphones and autos, while TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker.

items.title: JP Morgan raises S&P 500 year-end target to 8,000
items.summary: NEW YORK: JP Morgan on Monday raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 to 8,000, citing strong corporate earnings and signs that AI investments by hyperscalers are poised to generate faster revenue growth. The new target implies a roughly 3.12 per cent upside from the close of 7,757.64 points on Friday. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: High Court requests decision on venue for judicial review involving Negeri Sembilan Undang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The High Court has ordered counsel for three former Negeri Sembilan Undang and the incumbent Johol Undang to decide whether their judicial review will proceed here or Seremban, to avoid the risk of conflicting rulings on the same matter. High Court judge Norliza Othman’s directive follows an earlier originating summons filed by the applicants at the Seremban High Court in May, which has yet to be heard, The Edge reported. During the proceedings, the court also declined an oral application by Mohd Khairul for a gag order to prohibit public discussion of the case.

items.title: Five remanded another seven days over businessman's murder in Batu Pahat
items.summary: BATU Pahat: The remand of five men suspected of murdering a 39-year-old businessman, whose body was found wrapped in a net and floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, here last week, was extended. The case came to light after residents found the victim's body floating in the river at about 11.30am on Aug 3. Police also found five stones on the body, believed to have been used to weigh it down and prevent it from resurfacing.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah unveils RM12.3m Penang STEM programme, targeting 100,000 students by 2030
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The federal government will allocate RM12.3 million for a four-year STEM talent programme in Penang aimed at reaching 100,000 students by 2030. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the allocation will support the implementation of the Penang STEM Talent Blueprint, which was first introduced by Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow in 2024. The programmes were developed by Tech Dome Penang, Penang Math Platform, Penang Science Cluster and Penang STEM.

items.title: [UPDATED] Arul Kumar is new DAP Negri Sembilan chairman
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Nilai assemblyman and National DAP vice-chairman J. Arul Kumar has been appointed as the new Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman, effective today. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the state committee unanimously selected Arul Kumar after he stepped down from the position, which he had held for 22 years since 2004. Loke said Arul Kumar, previously the Negeri Sembilan DAP vice-chairman, was appointed in accordance with the party constitution.

items.title: 2027 Budget development proposals at final screening stage, says Akmal Nasir
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Economy Ministry is in the final stage of screening development proposals for the 2027 Budget, with submission to the Finance Ministry expected by mid-August. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the ministry was finalising its assessment before submitting recommendations for development allocations under the second rolling plan (RP2) of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). Akmal said the process involved several stages, beginning with the implementing ministries, before development allocations were coordinated and endorsed by the Economy Ministry.

items.title: Roman wreck carrying hundreds of amphorae found off Sicily
items.summary: ROME: Italian divers have discovered the 2,100-year-old wreck of a Roman ship off Sicily, piled high with hundreds of well-preserved amphorae, which were likely used to transport wine. The wreck, dubbed by Italy's Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli as "one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years", was found some three miles off the coast of Mazara del Vallo. Underwater fishermen Giacomo De Mola and Igor Bisulli described how they stumbled upon the wreck.

items.title: Anthony Loke steps aside after 22 years, Arul Kumar appointed Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 10 — Nilai assemblyman and National DAP vice-chairman J. Arul Kumar has been appointed as the new Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman, effective today. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the state committee unanimously selected Arul Kumar after he stepped down from the position, which he had held for 22 years since 2004. Loke said Arul Kumar, previously the Negeri Sembilan DAP vice-chairman, was appointed in accordance with the party constitution.

items.title: Decades on, Merdeka spirit still burns brightly among the elderly
items.summary: That nostalgia was also felt by a group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, as this year's National Month celebrations took them back to their childhood days and, although decades have passed, memories of celebrating Merdeka (Independence) remain fresh in their minds. The waving of the Jalur Gemilang and the sound of patriotic songs once again evoked memories of Merdeka celebrations among the group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, bringing back the nostalgia etched in their memories. With great enthusiasm, the senior citizens sang Merdeka-themed songs together, made Jalur Gemilang flags and took part in a flag-assembling game during activities held at the community centre, demonstrating that their love for the country has never faded with age.

items.title: Budget screening nears completion, Economy Ministry to forward 2027 development proposals to MoF
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 10 — The Economy Ministry expects to complete its screening of development expenditure proposals for 2027 by the middle of this month, before submitting its recommendations to the Finance Ministry (MoF), Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. He said the ministry is currently in the final stage of Budget screening as part of preparations for the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). Akmal said the Budget preparation process goes through several stages, including submissions from the respective implementing ministries.

items.title: 'Low-hanging fruit' projects can drive Sabah development, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The implementation of "low-hanging fruit" projects could serve as a strategic catalyst for Sabah's development, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Hajiji said the people had high expectations of enjoying the benefits of development without delay. Also present were Deputy Chief Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam and Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, state Cabinet ministers and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.

items.title: Meta will soon face another high-stakes trial in US
items.summary: WITH two convictions and nearly US$1 billion in damages already stacked up, Meta will face another trial starting this week about alleged harms to children in a case brought by four US states. The federal trial, one of the most consequential among a myriad of legal proceedings targeting social networks in the United States, will begin Wednesday with jury selection at a federal court in Oakland, near San Francisco. That jury awarded the teenager US$6 million.

items.title: [UPDATED] Mohamad: Myanmar willing to repatriate 5,000 refugees by ship
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Myanmar has expressed its readiness to take back 5,000 refugees identified by Malaysia for repatriation, including transporting them home by ship, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. "When I met Myanmar's new foreign minister, they expressed their readiness to take back the 5,000 by ship. "If they are from Myanmar, then they are Myanmar refugees.

items.title: 'I regret not buying Haikal his favourite robot toy' - father mourns drowned son
items.summary: Mohamad Khairudi Setapa, 42, said his son, Mohamad Haikal Ramzi, had become unusually quiet in recent weeks, a change from the cheerful boy who was close to his elder sister and younger brother. "Haikal had become quiet lately. Khairudi said he last saw his second of three children at about noon yesterday before Haikal left home to play with his friend.

items.title: Cashless for all: E-wallets now a national habit for Malaysians across generations
items.summary: It was Malaysians aged 35-44, whose usage jumped nine percentage points to 64 per cent, and those 45 and above, up four points to 44 per cent. Four years ago, e-wallets skewed heavily young. “Malaysia has moved beyond digital payment adoption to digital payment dependence.

items.title: Two boys reported missing last night found drowned at Pasir Gudang dam after overnight search
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Aug 10 — The bodies of two primary schoolboys, who had been reported missing since last night, were recovered at a dam here by Fire and Rescue Department personnel early this morning. Pasir Gudang fire and rescue station operations commander Haizrul Rahmad said a water rescue team recovered Mohammad Haikal’s body at a depth of two metres and a distance of three metres from the dam’s edge at 2.12am. Haizrul said the search and rescue operation, involving fire and rescue personnel from the Pasir Gudang and Skudai stations, ended at 3am.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat to debate Tabung Haji RCI report in special meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Special Meeting of the Dewan Rakyat to discuss and deliberate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report regarding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will be held tomorrow. The special meeting is scheduled to begin with an explanation session by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, who will present an explanation regarding the RCI Report, followed by a question and debate session by Members of Parliament (MPs). Last Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul agreed that the special parliamentary session on Tuesday would be held without breaks to provide sufficient time for MPs to discuss the TH RCI Report.

items.title: Two company directors charged with failing to pay RM193,306 in sales tax
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Two directors of a caster wheel manufacturing company were charged in the Sessions Court here today with seven counts of failing to pay RM193,306.28 in sales tax and penalties. The accused, Lim Hooi Cheng, 54, and Karen Loo, 40, appeared as summoned persons and pleaded not guilty to all charges after they were read before Sessions Court Judge Irwan Suainbon. They were charged under Section 26(9) of the Sales Tax Act 2018 for violating Section 26(5) of the same Act.

items.title: Alleged cartel boss Kinahan charged in Ireland
items.summary: DUBLIN: An Irish court on Sunday charged alleged cartel boss Daniel Kinahan with directing a criminal organisation and remanded him in custody after his extradition from Dubai on a government jet. He is alleged to be one of the leaders of a transnational group, known as the Kinahan Organised Crime Group (KOCG) or the Kinahan cartel. Irish police later said in a statement they had arrested and charged a man in his late 40s over "serious organised crime offences" without naming Kinahan.

items.title: Selangor to develop 'super app' for 12 local authorities
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government plans to develop an integrated application, or 'super app', that brings together the services and complaint channels of the state's 12 local authorities (PBT), State Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said. Ng said the initiative aims to speed up and simplify public dealings by providing access to various services of local authorities through a single platform. Ng said counter services of local authorities would not be discontinued to assist those who were less digitally literate, particularly senior citizens and rural residents.

items.title: Transboundary haze worsens as nine Sarawak areas record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 10 — The number of areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze rose to nine this morning. Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas were Kuching (161), Samarahan (161), Serian (179), Sri Aman (155), Sarikei (155), Sibu (158), Mukah (156), Bintulu (142) and Samalaju (141). API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Melaka election is change for PKR to rebuild, says Adam Adli
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 10 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) views the Melaka state election as a “new platform” to rebuild its strength through a more mature political approach centred on ideas and policies that are clearly communicated to the people. Acting Chairman of the Melaka PKR Leadership Council Adam Adli Abd Halim acknowledged that the party faces a major challenge in rebuilding public confidence after failing to win any state seats in the 15th Melaka state election in 2021. In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.

items.title: Woman escapes unhurt after car catches fire on Penang Bridge
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 3.07am about the incident at Km1.4 of the bridge, from the island towards Prai. He said firefighters from the Prai Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 3.16am, about 20km from the station, and brought the fire under control at 3.20am. John said the fire involved the vehicle's engine compartment, while the cause of the fire had yet to be determined.

items.title: Takiyuddin says PAS has no offers to join unity government, will await DAP’s decision
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — PAS secretary general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan declared the party has received no approaches or offers to join the unity government, stressing it will simply “wait and see” what happens when DAP decides its position on August 16. “For August 16, we will wait and see. We have not received any approaches or offers to join the government.

items.title: 8 teens charged with murder over fatal assault in Brisbane
items.summary: SYDNEY: Eight teenagers have been charged with murder over the fatal assault of a 21-year-old man in Australia's Brisbane late in July, reported Xinhua. A police statement said that detectives on Sunday arrested four males, three aged 18 and a 17-year-old, and charged them with murder. Police initially said that officers at the scene on July 26 observed significant damage to vehicles and a residence.

items.title: Zahid congratulates Malaysian men’s doubles pairs after Korea Masters one-two
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated men’s doubles pairs Tee Kai Wun-Yap Roy King and Soh Wooi Yik-Man Wei Chong for emerging as champions and runners-up, respectively, in the 2026 Korea Masters Badminton Championships yesterday. Kai Wun-Roy King emerged champions in their Korea Masters debut at the Yi Sun-sin Gymnasium in Asan with a 21-13, 21-18 win over compatriots Wooi Yik-Wei Chong in 31 minutes. This is the second time Malaysia has won the Korea Masters title, with Wooi Yik partnering Aaron Chia to lift the men’s doubles crown in 2024.

items.title: Parliament to debate Tabung Haji RCI report in special sitting tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — A Special Meeting of the Dewan Rakyat to discuss and deliberate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report regarding the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will be held tomorrow. The special meeting is scheduled to begin with an explanation session by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr. Zulkifli Hasan, who will present an explanation regarding the RCI Report, followed by a question and debate session by Members of Parliament (MPs). Last Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul agreed that the special parliamentary session tomorrow would be held without breaks to provide sufficient time for MPs to discuss the TH RCI Report.

items.title: Immigration Dept arrests Pakistani man over alleged use of official logo, warning lights on vehicle
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 10 — The Immigration Department detained a Pakistani man who is believed to have used the department's official logo and warning lights on a vehicle, less than 24 hours after a video of the incident went viral on social media. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the man was detained in a special operation conducted at 4.30pm yesterday at PV3 Platinum Hill Condominium, Setapak, following intelligence gathered from the viral video showing a vehicle bearing the Immigration Department logo being used by a foreign national. Zakaria said the Pakistani man was detained for allegedly committing offences under Section 12(1)(f) of the Passports Act 1966 and the Immigration Act 1959/63, while the Indonesian woman was detained under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.

items.title: Terengganu police call for restraint as residents vent fury after foreigner crime case fuels tensions
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 10 — Police have issued a stern warning to the public not to take the law into their own hands following the arrest of three Rohingya men suspected of sexually assaulting a woman with intellectual disabilities in Kampung Besut, Kemaman. According to Sinar Harian , Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said any excessive action could disrupt public order and jeopardise the ongoing investigation. However, Mohd Khairi confirmed the assembly dispersed peacefully following police engagement and explanations.

items.title: ‘Taking too long’: Man arrested after allegedly brandishing meat cleaver at delivery rider at Terengganu petrol station
items.summary: Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 55-year-old suspect was arrested at about 10pm last night at his home in Kampung Nibung here. “At about 4.30pm, while the 26-year-old victim was refuelling his motorcycle, the suspect arrived on a Honda Wave motorcycle. The suspect suddenly shouted at and scolded the victim for allegedly taking too long to refuel, but the victim ignored him.

items.title: Maintenance worker drowns after suspected fall into water tank at Kuala Langat power plant
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 10 — A contract worker drowned after he was believed to have fallen into a five-metre-deep water tank while carrying out maintenance work at the cooling tower of the Kuala Langat Power Plant in Kuala Langat here yesterday. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the incident at about 7.29pm before personnel were deployed to the scene. “The victim was carrying out maintenance work with a colleague to replace wood at the cooling tower before his colleague left to get more wood.

items.title: Nadi offers cheaper school uniforms for families, says education minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The Nadi School Uniform initiative not only helps families acquire school supplies at more affordable prices, but also opens up opportunities for alumni of the Nadi Sewing Skills programme to generate income through the skills they have learned. It is from this programme that the Nadi School Uniform initiative was born. Through its Lifelong Learning pillar, Nadi provides a platform for underprivileged and marginalised groups to access education and skills training, covering Nadi TINYTECHIE, NURTURE EKELAS Students, Nadi E-Sports, Nadi Rakyat Tuition, Nadi Cybersecurity, Nadi Skills (Sewing, Cooking, Gadget Repair, Photo/Video, Smart Agriculture, ICT Literacy), and the Nadi AI Programme.

items.title: Anwar undergoing medical checks, PMO confirms two‑day specialist observation period
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is undergoing medical examinations and procedures prescribed by a team of specialist doctors, his office confirmed today. Senior press secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said Anwar is expected to remain under observation for two days. The Prime Minister’s office did not disclose further details of the procedures.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah will use RM1.5b federal special grant for infrastructure and welfare
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 10 — All revenue received by Sabah from the Federal Government will be channelled back to the people through various forms of incentives, assistance and development, says Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. The Sabah state government was previously reported to have received RM600 million of the RM1.5 billion interim special grant payment disbursed by the Federal Government on June 12. Meanwhile, Hajiji said the state government continued to focus on financial performance and increasing revenue collection, with annual collections maintained at RM7 billion since 2022 and expected to increase to RM8 billion this year.

items.title: Police: Four masked suspects break into Sungai Buloh home, make off with RM35,000 worth of valuables
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — The police are actively conducting an investigation into a burglary case suspected to have been carried out by four masked suspects at a woman's residence in Sungai Buloh, Selangor, resulting in an estimated loss of RM35,000. Sungai Buloh district police chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said the report regarding the incident was received by the police yesterday. Mohd Hafiz said that members of the public who have information regarding the incident are requested to contact the investigating officer, Sergeant Shamie Yusop, at 013-6463069 or the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters at 03-61561222 to assist with the investigation.

items.title: Lim Lip Eng posts RM5,000 bounty after woman set alight in brutal Kepong petrol attack
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 10 — Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng has announced a RM5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of the suspect who doused a woman with fuel and set her alight in a brutal attack at Taman Pusat Kepong yesterday. Lim described the assault as “an act of shocking cruelty” and urged police to hunt down the attacker swiftly. Members of the public with details are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Muhammad Amri Firdaus Jusoh at 010 9198209, the Sentul district police headquarters at 03 40482222, or the nearest police station immediately.

items.title: Sabah to acquire 30pc stake in two new oil and gas fields, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 10 — The Sabah government will acquire a 30 per cent stake in two new oil and gas fields on the state's east coast, said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the state government was also finalising the acquisition of 40 per cent equity in the floating liquefied natural gas facility project in Sabah. Hajiji also said that the state government continues to focus on strengthening financial performance and increasing state revenue collection as an important foundation in driving Sabah's development.

items.title: Number forecast operator doused in petrol and set ablaze while working in Kepong
items.summary: Acting Sentul district police chief Supt Jasni Zolpa said the victim, 62, who worked as counter staff at the number forecast operator was attacked by the unknown suspect at 8pm “Preliminary investigations revealed the victim did not have any enemies nor received any previous threats. The Kuala Lumpur contingent police headquarters’ forensics team has also conducted further investigation at the scene of the crime and taken several samples of related items and deoxyribonucleic acid to assist investigations, he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code. He urged those with information on the incident to contact investigating officer, Insp Muhammad Amri Firdaus Jusoh at 010-9198209, the Sentul district police headquarters operations room at 03-40482222 or the nearest police station.

items.title: If police stop you in Malaysia, here's what you should know
items.summary: What if they ask you to follow them to the police station? Can police check your phone? A police officer stops you.

items.title: Pulau Tuba’s authentic village life pitched as Langkawi’s next big tourism secret
items.summary: LANGKAWI, Aug 10 — Pulau Tuba has the potential to attract more domestic and international tourists with its authentic traditional village atmosphere and unique cultural experiences, said Kedah Tourism, Culture and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Salleh Saidin. He said despite Langkawi recording more than three million tourist arrivals, visitor numbers to Pulau Tuba remained relatively low, highlighting the island’s untapped potential as a “hidden gem”. “Tourist arrivals in Langkawi reach the millions, yet only a small number visit Pulau Tuba.

items.title: National unity minister says Orang Asal heritage part of Malaysia’s national identity, not separate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The heritage of Malaysia’s indigenous peoples (Orang Asal) is part of the country’s national legacy and identity, rather than belonging solely to the communities themselves, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said. In a Facebook post marking the 2026 International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples today, he said efforts to empower indigenous communities should move in tandem with national development without allowing their languages, customs and traditional knowledge to become marginalised. “Malaysia is fortunate to have indigenous communities that are an important part of the country’s history and identity.

items.title: MBPP blames root rot and trunk cavity for Angsana collapse in George Town
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Root rot and a cavity in the base of a 90-year-old Angsana tree, compounded by chronic soil compaction and limited rooting space, contributed to its collapse along Jalan Macalister here today. MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the 28-metre-tall tree, Pterocarpus indicus, had an estimated 30 per cent root rot, while cavity decay accounted for about 40 per cent of its base trunk. He said MBPP had assessed mature and aged trees along Jalan Macalister in 2024, resulting in 13 trees being identified for felling, all of which had since been removed.

items.title: Sarawak chokes under haze blanket as hot weather grips state until Aug 14
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Most parts of Sarawak will be experiencing hot weather and reduced rainfall until August 14, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. In addition, southern Sarawak is set to experience transboundary haze due to increased hotspots in the neighbouring country, he said. “Analysis of the latest weather forecast models indicate that hot weather and below-average rainfall are expected in most parts of Borneo, including Sarawak, until August 14.

items.title: Terengganu police arrest three Myanmar men over sexual offence against disabled woman
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 9 — Three Myanmar male refugees working as construction and cleaning workers were detained in connection with a sexual case involving an intellectually disabled woman in this district yesterday. Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the three men, aged between 19 and 28, were arrested after receiving a report regarding the alleged sexual case from a 20-year-old woman on Friday. He said that the public is advised not to make any baseless speculation as the case is still under police investigation.
